- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 2–3 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40–45), model tends to hold or overestimate; adjust downward by 3–7% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +0.7 to +0.8), model often lags; anticipate 1–2 day delay in price reaction; add 1–2% lagged adjustment.  
- If model forecast is consistently >45 for 3+ days with no true price drop, consider “overconfident” bias; reduce by 5–8% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ days below 40), model often fails to recognize; apply downward bias of 3–6% for next 5–7 days.
